_meta.note: All numbers were read from the fetched pages cited. null means not found.

idio_vol.description: Annual standard deviation of an individual house's return beyond the metro/national index. Older literature gives about 14-15%/yr total individual-house volatility, against about 4-6%/yr for city indices. Newer resale-based studies estimate an idiosyncratic component of about 9-18% that is roughly flat in holding period: a one-time (transitory) shock, not a random walk.

estimates.source_title: Flavin & Yamashita (2002), 'Owner-Occupied Housing and the Composition of the Household Portfolio', American Economic Review 92(1):345-362
estimates.definition: Annual s.d. of individual-house real return (PSID, 1968-1992); Table 1A gives 0.1424. Case-Shiller city indices give 0.042-0.065.
estimates.quote: the standard deviation of the return to housing, at the level of the individual house, is about 0.14

estimates.source_title: Case & Shiller (1987/1989), 'The Efficiency of the Market for Single-Family Homes', NBER WP 2506 / AER 79(1)
estimates.definition: Total annual variability of individual house prices
estimates.quote: close to 15% a year for individual housing prices

estimates.source_title: Giacoletti (2021), 'Idiosyncratic Risk in Housing Markets', Review of Financial Studies 34(8):3695, doi:10.1093/rfs/hhab033 (job-market-paper version)
estimates.definition: Volatility of the transitory idiosyncratic shock (Table 8). The persistent random-walk component is small (sigma_v 0.0015-0.036). The term structure is flat, so the shock does not grow with holding period. Idiosyncratic risk is up to 60% of capital-gain volatility at a 1-yr holding period, under 20% at 5 yrs, and about 5-10% at 10 yrs. Metro index annualized volatility is about 4-5%.

estimates.source_title: Gan, Wan & Xu (2024 draft), 'It is Not Easy Being a Flipper' (Hong Kong, 1993-2021)
estimates.definition: Mean annualized idiosyncratic s.d.: 9.32% by the Giacoletti method, 9.27% by the Peng-Thibodeau method. It declines about 0.6 pp per extra holding year.

estimates.source_title: Sagi (2021), 'Asset-Level Risk and Return in Real Estate Investments', RFS 34(8):3647, doi:10.1093/rfs/hhaa122 (commercial real estate)
estimates.definition: Commercial properties. Variance = intercept (about 20% s.d., independent of horizon) + 10%/yr annualized random-walk slope. The paper says the findings are qualitatively similar to residential studies (Case-Shiller 1987, Goetzmann 1993).
Undiversified single-home annualized volatility of 15%/yr versus 4% diversified

idio_vol.notes: Modeling choice: model the idiosyncratic shock as about 10-15% s.d. realized at sale (horizon-independent, per Giacoletti/Sagi), or as about 14%/yr total volatility if using the older random-walk framing. Peng & Thibodeau was not fetched directly; its value comes only through Gan et al.

tenure.description: NAR 2025 Profile: sellers' median tenure was 11 years, an all-time high. Redfin: the typical homeowner stayed 12 years in 2025, up from 11.8 in 2024. Census CPS Table A-4: 4.1% of owners moved in 2023, the lowest in the series since 1988; 16.2% of renters moved.

sources.title: NAR, Top 10 takeaways from NAR's 2025 Profile of Home Buyers and Sellers
HomeSnacks, citing Census CPS Historical Geographic Mobility Table A-4
Census CPS Table A-4 (xlsx; could not be parsed directly)
Harvard JCHS, household mobility fell to record low in 2024

tenure.source_title: NAR 2025 Profile of Home Buyers and Sellers; Redfin 2026; Census CPS Table A-4
tenure.notes: The owner mover rate of 4.1% implies a mean stay of about 24 yrs under a constant hazard, which is longer than median seller tenure because tenure is right-censored and heterogeneous. The 4.1% figure comes via HomeSnacks' reading of Census Table A-4; the xlsx itself could not be parsed. JCHS reports owners under 45 at 9.8% in 2024 (ACS).

div_yield.notes: The 2026-10-21 value is an estimate based on 12-month dividends through June 2026 (S&P). Year-end history is from https://www.multpl.com/s-p-500-dividend-yield/table/by-year. The long-run mean is 4.20%.

zori.description: Zillow Observed Rent Index, national. Values are January snapshots 2015-2025 (smoothed, all homes plus multifamily), plus December points found in Zillow reports and the latest 2026 figure.
zori.source_title: keepingupwithinflation.com rent tracker (ZORI, January snapshots); Zillow monthly rent reports; Zillow September 2026 Market Report
zori.notes: Full December 2015-2025 series not found: the Zillow CSV (files.zillowstatic.com) could not be read via WebFetch. The January series is from a third-party tracker of the smoothed ZORI, so its levels differ from the December points in the raw/seasonal report series (e.g., Dec-2024 $1,965 vs Jan-2025 $1,882); do not mix them. The YoY rates are the most usable figures. Multiply January-to-January growth 2015-2025: 1882/1155 = 1.629, about 5.0%/yr.

mortgage_annual.description: Annual average of the Freddie Mac PMMS 30-year fixed rate (%).
mortgage_annual.source_title: Freddie Mac PMMS, annual average of weekly 30-year fixed rates
mortgage_annual.notes: I verified 2021-2025 by averaging Freddie Mac's weekly archive values: 2021 = 2.958, 2022 = 5.344, 2023 = 6.807, 2024 = 6.721, 2025 = 6.595 (53 weeks). They match this table. Rocket Mortgage gives the same table for 1972-2024 (1981 = 16.64) but 6.47 for 2025, which is wrong against the Freddie weekly data; use 6.60. A Bankrate table (wlox.com) differs from 1982 onward because it uses Bankrate's own survey, so do not use it. 2026 weekly rates rose from about 6.0% (Feb-Mar) to 7.40% (Oct 8 and 15, 2026). 1981 corrected to 16.64 after independent audit (mean of 53 weekly FRED values = 16.6415).

margin_rate.description: Interactive Brokers Pro USD margin rates: benchmark + 1.5% (up to $100k), + 1.0% ($100k-$1M), + 0.75% ($1M-$50M). The benchmark implied by the tiers is 3.88%.
margin_rate.notes: Fetched 2026-10-22; the page itself carries no date. The benchmark is not named on the page (IBKR's USD benchmark is normally Fed Funds effective). Box-spread rates (about Treasury/SOFR + small spread) were not found as text; the SyntheticFi Q2 2026 chart is an image only. For a calculator, benchmark + 0.5-1.5% is realistic.

mortgage_spread.description: Long-run average spread of the 30-year fixed mortgage rate over the 10-year Treasury yield
mortgage_spread.source_title: First American, 'Mind the Gap Between Mortgage Rates and the 10-Year Treasury Yield' (Odeta Kushi, 2023-05-24)
mortgage_spread.notes: First American: on average 1.7 pp (170 bp) since the end of the Great Recession. HousingWire FAQ: historically about 1.7-1.8 pp, with spreads above 2% more common in recent years.

sell_costs.description: Commission after the NAR settlement is about 5-5.5% combined (Opendoor citing Redfin). Redfin's average buyer-agent commission was 2.40% in Q1 2025 and 2.42% in Q3 2025. Seller closing costs other than commission are 1-3%. Opendoor's all-in figure of 10-15% also includes repairs, staging and moving.

sources.title: Opendoor, How Much Does It Cost to Sell a House in 2026?
Redfin, real estate commissions May 2025 (Q1 2025: 2.40% buyer agent)
MortgagePoint, Redfin Q3 2025 buyer agent commission 2.42% (2025-12-31)

sell_costs.source_title: Opendoor 2026 cost-to-sell guide; Redfin commission reports
sell_costs.notes: total_seller_typical = 0.07 is a derived suggestion (about 5.5% commission + about 1.5% closing), not a quoted figure; 6-8% is the realistic range. The commission data show that buyer-agent fees are still about 2.4% after the settlement.

buyer_closing.description: Buyer closing costs of 2-5% of purchase price. ClosingCorp reports an average of about $6,800 for a single-family home (year not stated).
buyer_closing.source_title: The Mortgage Reports, Average Closing Costs 2026 (2026-01-16)
buyer_closing.notes: $6,800 on a roughly $400k median home is about 1.7%. 2-3% is a reasonable central value including lender fees and prepaid items.

maintenance.description: Census 2021 AHS (homes built before 1950): median spending on improvements plus maintenance was 1.5% of value for new owners (in the home under 2 years) and 0.6% for longtime owners (10+ years). More than half spent under 1%. Routine maintenance alone had a median of about $540/yr. The industry rule of thumb is 1-3% of value per year.

sources.title: U.S. Census Bureau, 'Cost of Improving and Maintaining Older Homes Higher for New Owners' (Oct 2023, 2021 AHS)
HomeLight, average home maintenance costs (NAHB $950/yr from 2019 AHS; Angi 2020 $3,192/yr; Porch 2021 $9,820/yr; rule of thumb 1-3%)
PearlScore home maintenance cost report 2026 (Bankrate-based $8,808/yr in 2025)

maintenance.notes: Estimates vary widely with definition (routine vs including improvements). 1% of value/yr is defensible for maintenance plus repairs; 1.5% if capital replacements are included.
